significance.justification: A verified-true result would establish that, in a distinguishable class of wrong answers, a fact is "encoded in mid-layer representations but never gets copied into the residual stream at the answer position," and that causally restoring this transfer repairs factual use; this is a form-(ii) causal mechanism plus a behavioral phenomenon, not a form-(iii) law. It would constrain error attribution by predicting that decodable-but-unrouted cases respond to the "retrieval nudge" whereas genuinely absent facts do not, a meaningful distinction for causal-localization and editing work such as Meng et al.'s ROME and representation-extraction methods such as Patchscopes, but it remains bounded mainly to one failure class rather than fixing behavior across unrelated knowledge failures. The negative branch would rule out mid-layer decodability plus failed subject-to-answer transfer as a useful storage/retrieval decomposition, although "primarily," "reliably," and "partially fixable" lack quantitative bounds; true and false nevertheless denote reasonably distinct worlds because the claim also requires separability and causal repair. Topic-substitution check: the broad topic alone would not earn this score—the specific copy-failure mechanism and selective repair add real constraint beyond merely asking why stored knowledge is not used—but their familiar probe-plus-causal-intervention shape keeps the result near the topic median.

reach.justification: The claim names two usable handles: a "classifier on internal features to predict, before generation, whether the model will exhibit a retrieval gap" and a runtime, query-agnostic "retrieval nudge." The classifier is explicitly ex ante and leaves an action window for auditors or deployment systems to flag, gate, reprompt, or intervene before the answer, while the nudge is itself a pre-output intervention rather than merely a post-hoc explanation. After recalibration on another model, however, the conclusion supplies a procedure for finding a model- and fact-dependent decoding direction rather than a scaling law, threshold, or invariant relation predicting what the new model will contain; its asserted scope covers factual, relational, paraphrased, and multi-hop queries, but cross-architecture robustness is not part of the mechanistic law. Topic-substitution check: deleting these specific pre-generation and runtime handles leaves only the general knowledge-retrieval topic, which would not justify this reach; the ex-ante diagnostic and potential uptake by model auditors support the higher band despite limited relation-level transfer.
